title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police used AI facial recognition to wrongly link her to bank fraud. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail without bail, then about two more months in North Dakota. Charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time. Lipps lost her home, car, and belongings, and says she was denied medications and dentures while in custody.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million, alleging false arrest, malicious prosecution, and lack of police training or supervision on facial recognition technology. The lawsuit says the software matched her social media photo to a fake ID used by a suspect, but officers did not verify the lead or establish probable cause. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The case seeks damages and accountability, with no further court dates mentioned in the article.
